title: Activepieces Open Source License: What Is Free (2026)
summary: Activepieces open source license is MIT, permitting you to use, modify, and distribute the software commercially with minimal restrictions.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces Self-Hosting and the Paid Line


Read the line before rollout, not after: the Community Edition is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, while SSO beyond Team, audit logs, embedding and self-hosted enterprise deployment sit behind paid plans.


### What the Community Edition includes


The core is MIT, and the point where it stops is written down: the LICENSE file in the activepieces/activepieces repository puts` packages/ee/` under a separate commercial licence and everything else under MIT.


Outside that directory, MIT's permissions apply in full, so you can run the code, fork it, sell it or ship it inside your own product without a fair-code clause to read first, whereas a source-available licence like n8n's lets you read the code and keeps those rights with the vendor, as this[n8n vs Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/activepieces-vs-n8n) comparison explains.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The[Activepieces team on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ashrafsam_400-pieces-by-300-contributors-just-activity-7371636480894640128-3ccq) put the library at 280 integrations in March 2025 and 285 in June. It reached 400 by September and 500 by November.


**The jump of 215 in five months** means a gap you found in spring may be closed, so recheck before ruling a tool out.


To self-host, work through these steps in order:


1. Follow the documented Docker-based setup on a server you control.
2. Set the environment variables the docs list for your instance.
3. Start the stack and create the first account.


Once it runs, patching, backups and uptime are yours. When the vendor's cloud is down, yours is unaffected, but when your server is down, nobody else fixes it.


### Which features need a paid plan


The pricing page shows Free at $0 with 1,000 credits a month, and Plus at $20 flat per month. Exceeding 1,000 monthly credits therefore requires the $20 Plus plan.


Team is $200 a month, and Ultimate is by quote, with cloud or on-prem deployment, custom roles and dedicated support. **Custom roles are an Enterprise item** , so a team needing them can't rely on the free edition.


For cost,[SaaSSwitcher](https://www.saasswitcher.com/blog/make-alternatives) priced 10,000 monthly tasks at $20 on[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , $55 on Make and $129 on Zapier.


Its $20 differs from the $25 Plus list price, so treat the comparison as directional and confirm on the pricing page. Even so, the cheapest of the three is under a sixth of the dearest.


SOC 2 is in progress, not certified, so a buyer who needs the report today can't have it. If you want no servers to maintain and no licence questions, a hosted plan is the cleaner choice.
